Live Updates: Houthis threaten U.S. with "swift and painful" response if it joins Saudi Arabia's strikes on Iran-backed group
Duarte Pita Dias is based in CBS News' London bureau, where he works across digital platforms and for TV broadcasts.
Frank Andrews is a CBS News journalist based in London.
Updated on:  October 13, 2026 / 2:23 AM EDT
What to know about the Iran war today:
A Houthi official said Monday there would be a "swift and painful" response if the U.S. joins Saudi Arabia's strikes against the Iran-backed group, after President Trump said he was considering joining the offensive.
At least 20 people, including a U.S. national, have been killed in a week of Houthi

The price of Brent crude oil, the international benchmark, climbed back to a two-week high over $105 a barrel Monday after President Trump said Saturday that he was

Houthis threaten U.S. with "painful" response if it joins Saudi Arabia's offensive
A Houthi official threatened the U.S. on Monday with a "swift and painful" response if it joined Saudi Arabia in striking the Iran-backed group.
Following an attack at the Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia on Saturday that killed 13 people, President Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group. He had  reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom.
"The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. They're misbehaving very badly. No good," Mr. Trump said on Monday.
"If the U.S. becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the U.S. and all its interests in the region," Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told the Agence France-Presse news agency in an interview.
He also warned "all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports (should) stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets".

5:50 PM / October 12, 2026
Saudis investigate why deadly strike on Riyadh airport wasn't intercepted
Saudi Arabia has launched an investigation to determine how its air defenses failed to intercept a barrage of missiles and drones fired by Iran-backed Houthi rebels, including an attack on Riyadh airport that killed at least 13 people and wounded over 300, two regional officials said Monday.
The officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly, said the initial probe showed that Yemen's Houthis first fired multiple drones to pave the way for a mix of cruise and ballistic missiles to reach Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport.
The Houthis possess ballistic missiles and advanced systems fitted with warheads that can change direction during flight and pose a challenge to Patriot interceptors and other defense systems used by the Saudis.
One of the officials said the investigation also aims to find out why air defense systems did not provide earlier warning of the attack in which the Houthi missiles and drones flew over 620 miles to reach Riyadh.

5:19 PM / October 12, 2026
Delta delays planned flights from Atlanta to Riyadh amid attacks on airports
Delta Air Lines said Monday it is delaying plans for nonstop flights from Atlanta to Riyadh amid escalating attacks between Yemen's Houthi militants and Saudi Arabia.
"The safety and security of our customers and employees always come first and continue to guide our operational decisions," the company said in a statement. "We remain in close contact with relevant government and aviation partners, including Saudia and Riyadh Air, as we monitor the situation."
its plans to operate nonstop flights to Riyadh three times a week on its Airbus A350-900 aircraft in October 2026. It said at the time that the new destination would help strengthen business and travel ties between the United States and Saudi Arabia.
The company said Monday the launch of Atlanta-Riyadh flights will take place in March 2027.

Iran's foreign ministry says U.K.'s accusations are unfounded
Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday denied the U.K.'s allegations that Tehran was involved in last month's security incident at a British base used by American bombers.

In its response, Tehran said by using terms like "highly likely" and "almost" certain, the U.K. is "hiding behind vague language without presenting concrete evidence or proof."

NATO countries issue joint statement on Iran and RAF Fairford security incident
Foreign ministers of NATO member countries on Monday
condemning "Iran's use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners."
The statement said the countries recognize the U.K.'s assertion that last month's
security incident at RAF Fairford
, a U.S.-run air base in Britain, was likely coordinated by Iran.
"Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable," the joint statement said. " Anyone who conducts hostile activities on behalf of Iran, or any other state, should know that we will take action to identify, investigate, disrupt, and prosecute these acts."
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said
he welcomes the statement issued by allies and partners, echoing their denouncement of "Iran's involvement in violence and threats on Allied territory."
"NATO will continue to do its part to safeguard the security of our one billion people across the Alliance," Rutte said.

3:39 PM / October 12, 2026
Houthis confirm they targeted Riyadh's airport again with ballistic missile
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed an attack targeting Riyadh's international airport on Monday, after a Saudi-led coalition said it had shot down a missile over the capital.
"Our armed forces were able to target (King) Khalid International Airport in the Saudi enemy's capital Riyadh this evening with a ballistic missile and the hit was precise,"
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said
. He said the group also targeted the Khamis Mushait base in the kingdom's south with a drone.
Saree also warned against "the consequences of operating flights toward Saudi airports, as they are not safe, with the exception of the airports and airspace of the sacred areas in Mecca al-Mukarramah and Medina al-Munawwarah."
It's unclear whether there were any injuries.

2:40 PM / October 12, 2026
Multiple blasts heard in Riyadh, as residents warned of aerial threat
Several powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital Riyadh on Monday night, just moments after a text message sent to residents' mobile phones warned of an aerial threat.
"The area is under a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm, stay indoors or in a safe place away from windows and doors," read the message.
Around the same time, the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said its forces intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Iran-backed group at the capital.
"Interception and destruction of a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," Major General Turki al-Malki, a spokesperson for the coalition, wrote

2:05 PM / October 12, 2026
U.K. foreign minister announces sanctions against 2 Iranian nationals
U.K. Foreign Minister Ed Miliband announced sanctions against two Iranian nationals on Monday, "for their role in facilitating or engaging in hostile activity on behalf of the Iranian regime, with the clear intent of threatening, planning or conducting attacks overseas," he said in a
"We will not tolerate threats on British soil," said Miliband, who earlier had released a joint statement alongside his counterparts in the U.S., Australia, Canada and 23 other countries, which condemned hostile activities by Iran on foreign soil.
Their statements followed a security incident at the RAF Fairford air base in southern England, which U.K. government leaders and others have attributed to Iran. Iran denied its involvement Monday in comments released by state media.
https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-saudi-arabia-houthi/#post-update-1eafac06
1:35 PM / October 12, 2026
Americans detained for photographing attacks in Saudi Arabia, U.S. embassy says
The U.S. embassy in Riyadh said on Monday that American citizens had been detained for filming recent events in Saudi Arabia, which has suffered a string of deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
The embassy said "American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events," without specifying how many were arrested or whether they had been released. It noted that Saudi authorities have warned that "filming, publishing, or sharing information related to counter missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability."
Several foreign residents in Riyadh have told AFP that acquaintances were detained for filming recent events and sharing the footage on social media.
https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-saudi-arabia-houthi/#post-update-73838c49
1:24 PM / October 12, 2026
Iran denies involvement in U.K. air base incident, state media reports
Iran on Monday denied any involvement in a security incident at England's RAF Fairford air base, which the U.S. previously used to deploy long-range bombers during the war.
"The Iranian ambassador in London, Ali Moussavi, has again categorically rejected the accusations concerning Tehran's role in the incident at the Fairford military base," the Iranian state news agency IRNA reported, adding that he "called on the British government to present evidence supporting its allegations if it possesses any."
That statement followed earlier remarks from British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who said the incident was "almost certainly directed" by Iran's Revolutionary Guard.
https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-saudi-arabia-houthi/#post-update-e41b6792
12:43 PM / October 12, 2026
Iran claims to have struck 3 supertankers in the Strait of Hormuz in the last 2 days
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed Monday to have struck three supertankers in the Strait of Hormuz over the last two days.
The IRGC Navy said in its most recent attack on a ship, Monday, "a third non-compliant super-tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire."
It said the tanker had switched off the system that broadcasts a vessel's location in an effort to evade Iranian restrictions on navigating the strait without permission and "disregarded warnings from the IRGC Navy."
The statement warned that "any cooperation by commercial vessels and oil tankers with the invading, plundering American terrorist and smuggling army in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf region will be met with a decisive response from us."
President Trump and his senior aides have insisted for weeks that a southern route through the strait, skirting close to Oman's coast, is safe and available, and the U.S. military has escorted an increasing number of ships along that route in recent weeks.
Iran rejects that route and demands that all vessels use a northern passage close to its own coastline, seeking permission from its military.
The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center, which monitors incidents in the region, had not reported any attacks on vessels Monday, but it noted at least two projectiles hitting vessels Sunday.

11:53 AM / October 12, 2026
U.S., U.K., Australia, Canada and others condemn Iranian attacks, including "hybrid activities," after air base incident
The foreign ministers of the U.S., the U.K., Australia, Canada and 23 other countries, many in Europe, have released a
condemning hostile activities by Iran on foreign soil.
The statement came on the heels of British Prime Minister Andy Burnham saying a recent security incident at England's RAF Fairford air base, which was until recently home to U.S. long-range bombers, was "almost certainly directed" by Iran's Revolutionary Guard.
The countries said Monday that they "condemn in the strongest terms Iran's use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners."
incident to other recent attacks in Europe "targeting Jewish communities, Iranian journalists, and U.S. interests," the countries said: "Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable."
"Anyone who conducts hostile activities on behalf of Iran, or any other state, should know that we will take action to identify, investigate, disrupt, and prosecute these acts."

11:26 AM / October 12, 2026
U.K. prime minister says RAF Fairford air base plot "highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran"
at a British base used by American bombers to strike Iran during the ongoing war was "highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran" by the regime's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday.
British police have arrested and then released on bail seven men in connection with the alleged plot. The decision to free the men, whom British police say remain under investigation and monitoring, drew
criticism from President Trump
, who said in September the incident "might be" linked to Iran.
"I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard," Burnham told lawmakers in the U.K. Parliament on Monday.
"We will not tolerate these threats on our soil," he added. "We will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams."
Burnham said new sanctions against Iran would be announced.
https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-saudi-arabia-houthi/#post-update-0528376d
10:46 AM / October 12, 2026
Saudi Arabia vows response after deadly Houthi attacks on airports
Saudi Arabia's energy minister said Monday that the kingdom had been tested, but would mount an "equally serious" response to a string of deadly attacks on Riyadh's international airport by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels.
Lethal airport strikes have rocked the world's top oil exporter since last week, which is pursuing an expensive economic reform drive aimed at attracting foreign investment.
, in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Houthis, has reignited months into the U.S.-Iran conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.
"Energy security can't be taken for granted," Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told an energy conference in Riyadh. "The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious."
Operations remained suspended at the sprawling King Khalid International Airport on Riyadh's outskirts Monday after the weekend's deadly Houthi strikes.
CCTV video of the deadliest strike, which killed 13 people on Saturday, released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden flash tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.
https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-saudi-arabia-houthi/#post-update-b60057cd
10:12 AM / October 12, 2026
Saudi energy minister says petroleum summit shows kingdom still the "energy security capital," despite Houthi attacks
Saudi Arabia will continue implementing its economic goals and investing in energy infrastructure, industrial capacity and international partnerships despite the challenges presented by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said Monday.
Speaking at the World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh, the minister said Saudi Arabia had overcome major challenges throughout its history and would continue to do so, insisting that "fear has no place in the Saudi dictionary."
He said Riyadh's hosting of the international event reflected its position as an "energy security capital," adding that the participation of senior officials and experts from around the world showed international confidence in the kingdom and its ability to ensure the safety of visitors.
Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman chairs his delegations during the 17th Ministerial Meeting of the International Energy Forum (IEF), in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Oct. 11, 2026.
He spoke as the Saudi capital's main international airport remained shut down after a week of strikes by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen that killed 20 people.
The minister acknowledged that risks to the global energy system had not disappeared and he said that made international dialogue and cooperation essential to protecting supplies and stabilizing markets.
Bin Salman cited the East-West Crude Oil Pipeline as an example of Saudi long-term strategic planning, saying it provided an alternative route to transport oil amid ongoing impediments in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, and that it had helped the kingdom supply global markets during the exceptional circumstances of the war.
He credited state energy giant Saudi Aramco's expertise with helping restore operations quickly when disruptions do occur — which they have on multiple occasions during the U.S.-Iran war. Iran's proxy groups across the Mideast have targeted the East-West pipeline, along with other infrastructure, repeatedly, taking the pipeline out of service for weeks.

9:40 AM / October 12, 2026
Iran arrests lawyer behind death row marriage of protester, say rights groups
Iranian authorities have arrested a lawyer who helped organize and publicize a prison marriage between a young man who was executed the following day over the 2026 anti-government protests and his fiancee, who was also in jail, rights groups said Monday.
Alireza Sepahi, 25, and his partner Mahshad Kashani, 22, were married in a ceremony conducted over the telephone by their lawyer and attended by their fathers on the eve of
Sepahi's execution on Oct. 5
